title.narrative: Fiji bamboo to adapt and mitigate climate change

description.narrative: Active

The project aims to support the sustainable and inclusive production and use of bamboo as a resilient, sustainable and cost-effective construction material in Fiji that can be used to help increase the supply of affordable, resilient and accessible buildings in Fiji while also economically empowering women and other marginalised groups in Fiji. The project will seek to create an evidence-based enabling environment (the local capacity and policy environment) that will support and encourage: · the use of locally grown bamboo as a cost-effective, sustainable and resilient construction material in Fiji; · the environmentally sustainable (or even regenerative), socially inclusive and economically viable methods for cultivating, harvesting, treating and processing bamboo (for use in construction) in Fiji; and · women and other marginalised groups to seize the economic opportunities arising from the development of a new green and sustainable bamboo industry.

The project will aim to enable the uptake of locally suited bamboo species as a resilient material that can support climate change adaptation and provide livelihood opportunities for women/youth. It will combine: i) Knowledge generation and research on bamboo in Fiji, ii) Supporting building policies, iii) Training and capacity building; iv) Awareness initiatives on the use of bamboo as a sustainable building material to support the development of an enabling policy environment for bamboo to be used for construction. A focus shall be given to low-income resilient housing to provide suitable solutions for under-served communities, and for women-youth to play a protagonic role within the value chain (e.g. nurseries), as well as other potential income generation opportunities.
